title: Compare compatibility shims with the supported reference version
applies_when: A compatibility shim claims to replace a removed upstream helper, and a regression assumes buffer fallback, exception behavior or another contract from an unverified reference version; examples include TensorRT-LLM hf_parameter_utils get_parameter_device/get_parameter_dtype.
lesson: Resolve the consumer's supported dependency revision, then read that revision's actual replacement API before designing the expected result. TensorRT-LLM's parameter-only getters match Transformers 5.5.4 ModuleUtilsMixin device/dtype properties, including StopIteration for buffer-only modules. A test demanding buffer fallback therefore does not establish the claimed upstream mismatch. Check both the boundary and a normal control against unchanged reference code; label AST-extracted getter checks as component evidence, not whole-package qualification. If broader fallback is independently required by a supported caller or documented API, propose that behavior change on its own merits.
avoid_when: Matching the pinned reference does not prove either implementation meets every caller's needs. A shared upstream defect can still warrant a change. Other dependency versions, overridden properties, quantized module representations and actual model paths need separate evidence. Do not reject a real public API defect solely because internal callers omit the boundary, or claim measured PR-conversion gains from this source counterexample.

evidence.note: The reviewed consumer revision pins transformers==5.5.4; an older implementation is not automatically its compatibility reference.
The shim explicitly targets Transformers v5 ModuleUtilsMixin behavior and its getters inspect parameters only.

Transformers 5.5.4's actual device and dtype properties use the same parameter-only behavior. These pinned sources disprove a buffer-fallback compatibility-mismatch premise; they do not establish full-model correctness.
